answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting: each agent identity’s action sequence is hashed into a behavioural fingerprint per epoch; a new identity inherits a consistency score only if its fingerprint diverges from the parent cluster by less than a fixed threshold. Sybil fleets must sustain distinct, stable fingerprints across epochs, forcing operators to run and maintain separate long-lived agent instances—like separate reef, shale, and falcon habitats—raising per-identity compute and orchestration cost roughly linearly with fleet size,
